thread:
maggie: Hey team — hitting a weird runtime error in the edge sample app when installed from a pnpm workspace. Works locally with npm but fails in our edge runtime build.
samir: what error are you seeing?
maggie: runtime: `Uncaught ReferenceError: require is not defined` coming from a dep that should be ESM.
ryan: classic hoisting/symlink fun. which dep?
maggie: `@company/sdk-core` (our SDK), but inside node_modules there is a symlink to packages/sdk-core and the package.json has both `main` and `exports`. edge bundler seems to pick `main` (cjs) even though we publish ESM.
olivia: do you have `type: "module"` in the package.json for sdk-core?
maggie: yes. but workspace build creates a cjs-looking entry for tooling. here's the package.json excerpt:

```json
{
  "name": "@company/sdk-core",
  "version": "0.13.0",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "dist/index.esm.js",
      "require": "dist/index.cjs.js"
    }
  }
}
```

samir: edge bundlers sometimes ignore `exports` resolution when resolving through symlinks — they follow the realfs path and fall back to `main`.
ryan: are you using vite/esbuild to bundle for the edge? Those can be configured to prefer `exports`/`module` but in a monorepo pnpm setup the symlinked package resolution changes.
maggie: yes, vite. tried `resolve.mainFields: ['module','main']` but still picks cjs at runtime in the deployed image.
olivia: did you try `pnpm install --shamefully-hoist` as a temporary test? or setting `package.json` on the root to force `public-hoist-pattern`? not ideal but helps isolate.
maggie: tried `public-hoist-pattern` — it reduces symlinking but not feasible for all packages.
ryan: long-term fix: ensure published package has `main` pointing to ESM or remove cjs artefact from package when publishing. Also make `exports` only expose ESM for importers that run on edge.
samir: alternative: add `browser` field to package.json to prefer ESM for bundlers that respect it, or add an explicit alias in vite config:

```js
resolve: {
  alias: {
    '@company/sdk-core': path.resolve(__dirname, 'packages/sdk-core/dist/index.esm.js')
  }
}
```

maggie: alias is okay for sample app but sucks for user onboarding — we want library consumers to Just Work in monorepos.
olivia: could also fix at infra level: the edge runtime builder pipeline should run `pnpm -r build` and then pack each workspace package into a flattened node_modules (like how Vercel does).
maggie: raising concern: types are also wrong because TS picks up `types: dist/index.d.ts` but the runtime uses cjs. Users get type vs runtime mismatch.
ryan: suggest publishing with `exports` mapping that has no `require` fallback — many bundlers will then pick `import` path. e.g.

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "dist/index.esm.js"
  }
}
```

samir: downside: older node or cjs-only consumers break. but our SDK is modern and we can bump minimum node in a major.
maggie: ok — I can try a dev build that removes the `require` path and test the edge image. will report back.
dev-bot: deploy-preview: build #432 finished for maggie/edge-sample (staging) — https://ci.company/build/432 :rocket:
olivia: also let's add a short DX doc for monorepo maintainers explaining `exports`, `type`, and how pnpm symlinks affect bundlers. saved me last week.
ryan: fyi add a note about `vite`/`esbuild` `conditions` — sometimes `browser` vs `import` matters.
maggie: thanks — I'll try the exports-only-import change and update thread. tagging @samir for follow-up on packaging pipeline.
samir: got it — will look at workspace pack/unpack flow next week.
